blocks.heading: Decides What You Can Legally Call Yourself

items.text: The Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI) is the regulatory body that governs who can legally practise as a Clinical Psychologist in India.
To become RCI-registered, you need a UGC-recognised 4-year BA/BSc in Psychology with at least 55% marks (50% for SC/ST/OBC candidates), followed by the RCI-approved 2-year MA in Clinical Psychology.
Seats on RCI-approved MA Clinical Psychology courses are genuinely scarce - most universities currently offer around 10 seats per batch.

blocks.heading: Why Demand for Psychology Skills Keeps Climbing

items.text: None of this is a soft, feel-good claim about psychology being "important." It shows up as hard shortage data on the clinical side and real hiring demand on the non-clinical side.
India has roughly 0.47 registered clinical psychologists per 100,000 people, far below the WHO-recommended benchmark of about 1 per 20,000 (5 per 100,000).

Industry estimates put India's mental health sector growth near 16% a year as awareness rises, and one widely cited industry projection set a target of 3 lakh mental health professionals needed by 2025 - a marker already behind us, which underlines how far supply still lags demand rather than how the problem has been solved.

visuals.heading: Mistakes People Make Picking a Psychology Track

blocks.heading: It Usually Quotes Clinical or Counselling Salary

items.text: It rarely explains that RCI registration applies to only one of the six tracks, leaving people to assume the whole field needs a 7-8 year licensing process.
It skips the non-clinical tracks almost entirely, even though HR, analytics, and UX research are actively hiring psychology graduates right now.
It treats "scope" as a single yes-or-no question, instead of six separate answers that depend on which track you actually choose.

blocks.heading: Zones Test Before You Pick a Track

items.text: Clinical psychology - diagnosing and treating mental health conditions.
RCI registration is legally mandatory before you can call yourself a Clinical Psychologist or run clinical therapy.
The credential entry requirement is real: a specific RCI-approved degree, supervised clinical hours, then registration.
Assuming every psychology job needs RCI registration.
Committing to the 7-8 year clinical track without checking the current transition rules.
Picking "clinical" because it sounds most serious, without testing the daily reality.
Ignoring the non-clinical tracks because "psychology" sounds like only a therapy word.
Treating one salary number as the whole picture.
